description: A brief that is one bare fact and asks Stand to watch for nothing. Stand should keep the fact to itself until someone asks for it, or until a decision is about to rest on a different figure. The case is the user's own session of 2026-11-13: asked only "Stand, you there?", it answered "The team has 19 people." The lines that have nothing to do with the fact are followed by four seconds of quiet: with less, whatever Stand blurts out collides with the next speaker, is not played, and the run passes.

discussion.say: Yeah, let's start a discussion about this week's team outing activity.
Good. So I was thinking bowling, or maybe the escape room downtown.
Bowling is easier to book, I think. Let's go with bowling on Thursday evening.
Fine by me. I'll book lanes for twenty-five people, then.
Stand, how many of us are there again?
